scope: One already opened development apparatus, two nested evidence boundaries and two online agents. Not four independent discoveries, unseen-family transfer or a test of recursive superiority. Compilation and transfer are postponed.

trace.event: Authored analysis finds two exact threshold rules in its chosen state-model family.
Author selects the off=-0.4 predictor despite the unresolved off=-0.3 alternative.
Fresh confirmation returns two binary counterexamples in 96 new rows; MSE=1/48.
Author analyzes all 192 paid rows and finds only off=-0.3 compatible in its chosen family.
Author supplies new predictor source through evaluate(model,code); new paid MSE=0, incumbent paid MSE=1/96.
New 96-row confirmation passes; later 512-row terminal MSE=0.

online_revision.interpretation: Actual live counterexample-driven model replacement and renewed confirmation; no developer-written scientific source or mid-run guidance.

limitations: All four episodes concern one opened apparatus and two nested paid prefixes, not independent discoveries.
All four have zero prospective revisions, authored revision readouts and child questions. The scripted tests do not establish autonomous adoption.
The Hegel 72-row initial paired-path experiment does not distinguish its two surviving off thresholds; their resolution came from random confirmation.
Hegel used 30 calls and 354 new observations versus Code 14 calls and 192 new observations. No Hegel performance advantage is established.
There is no matched live before/after run, so live recovery cannot be attributed causally to a particular new connection.
Continuation-stage instructions were found ambiguous after the frozen run. Any subsequent clarification is outside this cohort source_at_run and has no measured benefit here.
